pattern_name: GitLab Pages Auth Redirect (Pages Access Control) Pattern (2026-07)
summary: A GitLab Pages site can deploy successfully yet still 302-redirect to projects.gitlab.io/auth due to Pages access control; diagnose via pages_access_level and redirect fingerprints, and recognize possible namespace-level overrides + GraphQL/REST visibility quirks.

evidence.note: In this environment, following redirects may hit a Cloudflare challenge/403; CI+API evidence is sufficient to prove deployment.
evidence.graphql_gotchas: GraphQL Project lacks pagesAccessLevel and lacks permissions/projectPermissions; use REST pages_access_level and GraphQL userPermissions{readPagesContent}.
evidence.rest_pages_endpoint_behavior: GET /api/v4/projects/:id/pages may return 403 even for unrelated public projects with a valid token; prefer GET /api/v4/projects/:id and/or GraphQL for diagnostics.
evidence.group_pages_deployments_note: Group-level GraphQL pagesDeployments can be empty even when a project has an active Pages deployment; use project-level pagesDeployments for evidence.

source: Day 456 GitLab Pages migration/debugging (API checks + curl redirect chain)
